html:
A Nigerian playwright, poet and essayist who in 1986 became the first African to win the Nobel Prize in Literature. He was born in Abeokuta into a Yoruba family and studied at Ibadan and at Leeds in England.

His plays blend Yoruba myth and ritual with European theatre. The best known include The Lion and the Jewel, A Dance of the Forests, written for Nigeria's independence in 1960, and Death and the King's Horseman (1975). He also wrote novels, poems and memoirs, among them Aké, about his childhood.

He has spent his life in conflict with Nigeria's rulers. During the Nigerian Civil War he tried to broker peace and was jailed for about two years, much of it in solitary confinement; he wrote about it in The Man Died. In the 1990s he fled the dictatorship of Sani Abacha and was sentenced to death in his absence. With Chinua Achebe he is the best known Nigerian writer of his generation.
